detail.title: DMGNet: Discriminative Multi-View Geometry Learning With Hybrid-Domain Enhancement for Light Field Occlusion Removal
detail.abstract: Light field captures rich spatial–angular information beneficial for occlusion removal. However, existing methods suffer from structural distortions, color shifts, blurred details, and artifacts, due to redundant information and noise, limited exploration of structure and texture details reconstruction, error propagation caused by inaccurate occlusion masks. To address these challenges, we propose DMGNet, a novel LF de-occlusion framework. Specifically, we propose a multi-view discriminative geometric–spatial aggregation module that aggregates rich geometric and spatial cues from all auxiliary views into the center view. The module adopts a new multi-view aggregation strategy and integrates spatial discriminative detail and channel discriminative detail attention to suppress noise and redundant information, thereby preserving key discriminative features. Subsequently, to achieve high-quality reconstruction of structures and texture details, DMGNet further introduces a multi-scale hybrid-domain collaborative enhancement module. At each scale, spatial enhancement enforces structural consistency, whereas hybrid-frequency interactive enhancement integrates global low-frequency context with local high-frequency details to reconstruct reasonable structures and high-fidelity details. Furthermore, a channel-specific mask confidence generator produces adaptive confidence maps to mitigate reliance on uncertain occlusion masks and reduce error propagation. Extensive experiments illustrate that DMGNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods on real and synthetic datasets.

title: The Path to the Singularity: An Ideological History
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Path to the Singularity: An Ideological History
detail.abstract:
This paper traces the deep historical and philosophical currents that have propelled human civilisation toward a ”Resource Entropy Singularity”1 —a point of no return where the biophysical demands of the global economy overwhelm and irreversibly degrade the planetary systems upon which we depend. This crisis is often viewed through a purely material lens, as a failure of technology, overpopulation, or poor resource management (Meadows et al., 1972). I argue, however, that its roots are fundamentally ideological, originating in a series of historical-philosophical breaks that systematically and deliberately redefined humanity’s relationship with the natural world (White, 1967) and, crucially, with the laws of thermodynamics.

This trajectory was not inevitable. It was the result of a specific worldview winning out over others, violently suppressing them, and then formalising its own assumptions into a supposedly "rational” and "scientific” system that rendered its own foundations invisible. This analysis traces this ideology from its mythological origins to its modern-day entrenchment, arguing that the current crisis is not a technical problem, but the logical end-point of a civilisational "operating system” (Daly, 1991) that is fundamentally at war with thermodynamic and biophysical reality.

This analysis begins by locating the ”original sin” of this trajectory not in a physical act, but in the foundational mythology of the West: the parable of Eden.

title: The optimal mechanism in high-frequency batch trading with multiple news

detail.title: The optimal mechanism in high-frequency batch trading with multiple news
detail.abstract: We develop a new high-frequency batch model based on game theory to analyze market behavior and address the issue of optimal trading strategies under multiple news arrival scenarios. In this framework, the behaviors and the profits of high-frequency traders (HFTs) are critically influenced by both the quantity and the sequence of news arrival. The model incorporates three interconnected games among HFTs and is refined to identify the trembling-hand perfect Nash equilibrium (THPNE). By maximizing the total market welfare measure, an optimal batch interval is determined to achieve the most efficient THPNE within the batch mechanism. Within this equilibrium, we characterize the optimal spread strategy and dynamic order strategy of HFTs. Single- and multi-period batch models are constructed to compute payoff matrices by analyzing market microstructure and HFTs’ behavior across multiple sequential news arrival scenarios, thereby enabling the derivation of the market spread and HFT profits. Finally, we show the optimal batch interval, a key practical finding that balances operational efficiency with strategic advantage, thereby providing actionable insights for market design and participant strategy.

detail.abstract: This paper aims to analyze whether the installation of Pacifying Police Units (UPPs) in some slums (also called favelas) in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, resulted in an overflow of violence to neighboring areas. The key hypothesis is that when a crime crackdown policy is implemented in a community, rather than reducing illicit activity, it merely partially shifts it to other locations with similar characteristics. Using a Spatial Difference-inDifferences (SDID) estimator that allows the modeling of a possible spillover effect, we show that Police Districts (PDs) that received UPPs experienced a decrease in drug trade-related crime, including rates of intentional homicide, violent crime, and car thefts. On the other hand, the opposite effect occurred in neighboring PDs that did not receive UPPs.

title: Optimal carbon reduction strategies driven by subsidies in the integrated electricity and carbon markets with jump-diffusion price dynamics
affiliations: , Peking University - Guanghua School of Management, Beihang University and University of Shanghai for Science and Technology - Business School

detail.title: Optimal carbon reduction strategies driven by subsidies in the integrated electricity and carbon markets with jump-diffusion price dynamics
detail.abstract: The global energy system is undergoing a fundamental structural realignment, significantly reshaping market dynamics where high-emission fossil fuel power and low-carbon renewable energy now coex ist within an integrated electricity-carbon market. High-emission fossil fuel power and low-carbon renewable energy constitute an integrated electricity market. Fossil fuel-based electricity is charac terized by lower costs and a consistent supply despite its significant carbon emissions. Clean energy generation requires substantial investments and only offers intermittent power supply. The interplay between electricity and carbon prices affects energy companies’ profitability and subsequently impacts their decision-making in the integrated electricity and carbon market. Jump-diffusion uncertainties in electricity and carbon prices raise the question of how power enterprises can obtain optimal feedback control strategies in a competitive scenario. We construct a compound Poisson stochastic differen tial game model to explore how profit-maximizing power enterprises can control carbon emissions and achieve green transformation amidst market competition. We characterize the double price jump risks captured by compound Poisson processes and introduce jump-diffusion terms into state equations as constraints. We derive the optimal feedback control strategies by solving coupled HJB equations for power enterprises. By constructing integral operators based on the Lévy process, we obtain equilibrium electricity and carbon prices that incorporate the optimal feedback control strategies of all competing power enterprises. Our findings reveal that neglecting the double price jump risks leads to underes timating the equilibrium electricity and carbon prices. The compound Poisson stochastic differential game modeling resolves the underestimated optimal electricity production and the overestimated op timal abatement input and subsidy.

detail.abstract: Algorithmic pricing is rapidly revolutionizing commerce. Firms offering algorithmic pricing advice are proliferating in a range of industries. Kalibrate (retail gasoline), Rainmaker (hotels), RealPage (apartment rentals), and Rouse Services (equipment rental) are just a few examples. These third parties contract with multiple subscribing firms in the same industry, collect those firms’ confidential business data, including prices and sales, and recommend prices each firm should charge. This business model raises serious risks of harm to consumers. Antitrust law can address the most egregious of these risks: using a third party to orchestrate a hub-and-spoke price fixing conspiracy or an unlawful information exchange agreement. But if a third party unilaterally recommends supracompetitive prices, antitrust law will not protect consumers. Such is the risk of third-party pricing algorithms that federal, state, and city governments have proposed laws strictly regulating them. Some jurisdictions already have enacted such laws. But third-party pricing algorithms also deliver efficiencies to businesses. Regulations that eliminate those efficiencies will favor big firms that can provide their own pricing solutions and disfavor their smaller competitors. This article recommends a more nuanced approach. It proposes a concrete solution that would protect consumers from algorithmic pricing abuses but retain this technology’s legitimate benefits.

detail.title: Carbon Pricing, Green Investment, and Welfare in the Energy Transition
detail.abstract: We analyze the macroeconomic and welfare implications of alternative carbon mitigation strategies using an environmental Dynamic General Equilibrium (eDGE) model calibrated to the Spanish economy. The framework features both renewable (green) and fossil fuel-based (brown) energy, allowing us to compare the transitional and long-run effects of different policy instruments on emissions, economic activity, and welfare. We consider four mitigation strategies: increases in fossil fuel prices, subsidies to green investment financed by lump-sum taxation, emissions taxes with household rebates, and emissions taxes used to fund green investment. Within the model, front-loaded mitigation policies can substantially reduce emissions over the medium term, but achieving net zero emissions by 2050 involves non-negligible welfare trade-offs during the transition. Carbon taxes play a central role in reducing emissions, while policies that redirect emissions tax revenues toward green investment yield more favorable long-run welfare outcomes. The results also highlight the importance of policy coordination, as unilateral mitigation efforts deliver limited environmental benefits relative to their macroeconomic costs.

title: Pioneering Jurisprudential Convergence: A KPI-Based Framework for Shia-Hanafi Rapprochement in Islamic Law

detail.title: Pioneering Jurisprudential Convergence: A KPI-Based Framework for Shia-Hanafi Rapprochement in Islamic Law
detail.abstract: This study introduces an innovative KPI-based framework for assessing doctrinal convergence and divergence between the Hanafi and Shia (Jaʿfarī) legal schools, aiming to advance practical strategies for inter-sectarian rapprochement in Islamic law. Anchored in the Twelve-Pillar Framework for Comparative Jurisprudence (TPF-CJ), the model operationalizes 240 key performance indicators (KPIs) across diverse doctrinal domains including legal reasoning, ritual practices, civil law, and digital transformation. Employing an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, the research integrates qualitative doctrinal analysis with quantitative validation via Delphi surveys, regression, and principal component analysis. The findings reveal that, while both schools share a common scriptural foundation, the Shia tradition exhibits greater flexibility by emphasizing rational deduction (ʿaql) and the integration of maqāṣid al-Sharīʿah, and demonstrates a higher readiness for digital innovations (e.g., AI-driven analytics and blockchain) compared to the more traditional Hanafi approach. Drawing on the seminal works of MoghadasNian (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025; MoghadasNian et al., 2024; MoghadasNian et al., 2025), this framework not only bridges classical fiqh analysis with modern evaluative practices but also provides actionable insights for policy reforms, institutional efficiency, and sustainable inter-sectarian dialogue. Moreover, the model’s applications extend to sectors such as airline management and tourism, where digital transformation is integral to operational excellence.

detail.abstract: Problem Definition: US agricultural supply chains are arguably among the most efficient in the world, yet recent supply chain disruptions have exposed a fundamental lack of resilience. Some point to market concentration as one reason for this lack of resilience, but little empirical evidence supports this claim. In this paper, we develop a model to test the effect of market concentration in both supplier and retail markets on agricultural supply chain resilience. Methodology / Results: We measure resilience using the time it takes gross marginsthe difference between retail and wholesale prices-to return to their previous levels after a major disruptive event. We test our model using data from the US beef supply chain following the 2019 Tyson beef packing plant fire in Holcomb, KS, which temporarily removed about 6% of the beef supply from the market. Using an event-study approach, we find that supplier and retail concentration detract from resilience during the reaction phase of the disruption response, but improve recovery times by roughly 14.0% during the recovery phase.

detail.abstract: Price inflation rose dramatically in late 2021. While there were many potential causes, some point to rising minimum wages, and wage inflation, as perhaps the most important source of food-price inflation. There is a large body of research that studies the aggregate effects of minimum wages, but none consider the precise mechanisms that link higher food prices and minimum wages in an environment of high general price inflation. In this study, we investigate the possibility that general price inflation serves as a facilitating mechanism for localized price inflation. We estimate both reducedform and structural models of minimum-wage pass-through. Reduced-form models show that general price inflation has a positive effect on minimum wage pass-through to retail food prices. However, reduced-form models cannot account for the effects of demand curvature and imperfect competition. Our structural model shows that, after controlling for the primary determinants of wage pass-through, general price inflation has an important role in accentuating the rate of minimum-wage pass-through. Our findings have important implications for minimum wage policy, and for understanding the role of labor cost in retail price inflation.

detail.abstract: Consumers tend to choose the type of store, or grocery channel, on the basis of "destination categories," or categories that tend to be important attractors relative to others. Whether or not a category is truly important to generating incremental market share, however, is a difficult empirical question, because there has been little exogenous variation that permits a clear test of whether categories tend to attract traffic. In this study, we leverage a change in beer distribution laws in the state of Colorado that permitted full-strength beer to be sold for the first time in traditional supermarkets. We use a difference-indifference estimation strategy to test whether the introduction of a new category of products represented an incremental gain in channel-attraction using both consumer panel and retail scanner data. Our results show that the introduction of beer into grocery stores in Colorado led to an increase in total weekly sales (1.2%), and a relative increase in expenditures for some categories, notably those that are likely to be complementary to beer purchases. Additional results using the consumer panel indicate an increase in the frequency of grocery store visits by beer-purchasing households as well as an increase in monthly grocery store expenditures (8.0%) among beer-purchasing households.

detail.abstract: This literature review asks: How can the views of classic thinkers—Max Weber, Philip Selznick, and Peter Drucker—be applied to downsizing policies that prioritize financial performance over employees? It proceeds in three steps. First, it summarizes contemporary evidence on the rationales and outcomes of downsizing. Second, it develops three interpretive lenses based on Weber’s theory of bureaucracy, Selznick’s institutionalism, and Drucker’s ethics of managerial responsibility. Finally, it synthesizes these perspectives into an integrated view of when financially motivated downsizing is likely to create versus destroy value in both an economic and institutional sense.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the formation and anchoring of long-run inflation expectations under bounded rationality and adaptive learning. The empirical analysis applies this framework to India, which provides a useful setting given its recent transition to a formal inflation-targeting regime. Motivated by the persistence of elevated term premia in India's sovereign bond market, we develop and estimate a New Keynesian model in which agents update beliefs about long-run inflation in response to short-horizon forecast errors, implying that expectations may remain imperfectly anchored even under an explicit inflationtargeting regime. The model is estimated using inflation data and survey-based short-run inflation expectations from India, allowing us to recover quarterly movements in ten-year-ahead inflation expectations. We find that the introduction of inflation targeting lowered the level of long-run inflation expectations and moved them closer to the policy target. However, long-run beliefs remain sensitive to short-run inflation surprises, consistent with adaptive learning and incomplete anchoring. This persistent belief updating generates long-horizon inflation uncertainty, which is priced into nominal bond yields and contributes to elevated term premia at longer maturities. Counterfactual simulations show that fully anchored expectations would substantially reduce long-horizon inflation uncertainty and lower long-maturity term premia by around 120 basis points. The results highlight how bounded rationality in expectation formation can sustain inflation risk and term premia despite improvements in monetary policy credibility.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes how the U.S.–China trade war affected Korean industries and identifies the industry characteristics that determined which industries gained or lost. I show that heterogeneity in responses is closely linked to capital intensity and export intensity, highlighting the role of economies of scale and export readiness. Using detailed industry-level data from Korean manufacturing, the analysis finds that capital-intensive industries with substantial pre-war investments and industries with high export intensity achieved greater growth and cost reductions following the tariff shocks. A publicly accessible retail dataset was examined to see how transactional features, product categories, and demographic information affected consumer behavior. To find significant trends, statistical techniques and basic predictive models were applied after the data was preprocessed and investigated using exploratory data analysis (EDA). The results show different spending trends for different product categories and genders, as well as category-level information that might help with datadriven retail decision-making. This study offers a useful foundation for retail analytics applications and shows how easily accessible machine learning methods can be utilized to extract valuable consumer information.

detail.title: Stablecoins and the DeFi-TradFi Entanglement: Systemic Risk and Connection Conditions
detail.abstract: The integration of decentralized finance (DeFi) and traditional finance (TradFi) through fiat-backed stablecoins has created a composite financial system exposed to new channels of systemic risk. This Article analyzes how arbitrage breakdowns, synchronized outflows, and thinning liquidity can interact to amplify selling pressure and trigger regime shifts that spill into short-term funding markets. Building on ideas from traditional market structure and regulation, it translates familiar tools into seven design principles for minimizing tail risk and then examines the distinctive constraints that arise when those principles are implemented through DeFi architectures such as automated market makers, lending protocols, and bridges. Recognizing that core DeFi protocols often lie beyond direct supervisory reach, the Article advances a regulatory strategy centered on "connection conditions" at supervised junctions. By tying access to banks, custodians, and centralized exchanges to clear standards for governance, risk management, and architecture, this strategy combines benefits and constraints so that Law, Market, Norms, and Architecture work together to align profit-seeking with financial stability and to replace opaque de-banking with a transparent pathway for safe DeFi connectivity.

detail.abstract: Using detailed Norwegian data on earnings, education and work histories, we estimate a dynamic structural model of education and sector choices that captures rich life-cycle patterns by individual ability. We validate the model against causal estimates of earnings returns and variation in education choices induced by a compulsory schooling reform. Using the structural model, we estimate ex-ante returns to different education tracks across the life-cycle by ability and quantify the contribution of option values. We find substantial heterogeneity in ex-ante returns and crucial role for option values at specific schooling margins. We assess how reenrollment possibilities and sectoral job opportunities influence track choices and derive predictions regarding the impacts of hypothetical educational policy reforms.

detail.abstract: In many Latin American countries, women disproportionately bear the burden of unpaid caregiving, potentially increasing their vulnerability to domestic violence. This paper investigates whether reducing unpaid care responsibilities can influence the incidence and severity of violence against women (VAW). I study the staggered rollout of Bogotá's Care Blocks-the first large-scale public care infrastructure in Latin America and the Caribbean-designed to provide free services to women caregivers and their dependents. Leveraging geographic and temporal variation in the implementation of Care Blocks across cadastral zones, I estimate their causal effect on reported VAW incidents using a dynamic differencein-differences framework. To measure severity, I develop a Natural Language Processing (NLP) classifier that analyses over 370,000 emergency call transcripts, identifying high-risk cases based on weapons, threats, injuries, and indicators of victim vulnerability. The findings show that Care Blocks increase the number of VAW-related calls by 68 percent relative to never-treated areas, with statistically significant effects emerging within five months of implementation. However, I find no corresponding change in high-risk reports-those signalling imminent danger to the victim. These results suggest that care infrastructure can reduce informational and logistical barriers to reporting violence but may have limited effects on structural or psychological constraints that inhibit reporting of severe abuse.

title: The Impact of Generative AI Adoption on Organizational Networks: Evidence From A Field Experiment

detail.title: The Impact of Generative AI Adoption on Organizational Networks: Evidence From A Field Experiment
detail.abstract: While generative AI (GenAI) tools can boost individual productivity, their effects on intra-organizational networks for collaboration and knowledge sharing remain largely unknown. We theorize that adopting GenAI reshapes employees' interaction patterns by acting as a translator (making collaboration easier) and as a knowledge catalyst (increasing the value of individuals as sources of knowledge), thereby rewiring interactions. We further propose role-based differences in these effects across specialists (deep experts) and generalists (broad integrators). We test these ideas in a randomized field experiment with 316 employees at a European technology services firm, randomly assigning 42 teams to either use a GenAI assistant customized with organization specific knowledge (treatment) or continue as usual without it (control). After three months, employees with the GenAI tool became significantly more central in their collaboration and knowledge-sharing networks than the control group, reflecting expanded ties and more frequent knowledge exchange. Specialists (technical support personnel) experienced greater increases in knowledge centrality than generalists (sales staff), while generalists gained the most in terms of performance, measured as number of projects executed. These findings provide causal evidence that GenAI adoption can rewire organizational social structure and augment performance differentially.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a unified rational framework integrating objective moral realism, metaphysical necessity, and cosmological coherence into a single logical system based in Observable Reality. Beginning with the empirical observation that teleology(purpose) and moral order are intrinsic to life and consciousness, the theorem suggests that these internal principles are consistent reflections of an outer universal order. This order, evidenced by the fine-tuning of the cosmos, logically requires a Non-Contingent, Infinite Ground that transcends space and time. The theorem concludes that a being possessing the properties traditionally ascribed to God (Unity, Necessity, Moral Perfection, and Creative Will) emerges as the most metaphysically necessary conclusion. The framework demonstrates that misalignment with this moral order produces predictable and observable decay (“Sin” to Disorder), positioning morality as a foundational, testable law of existence. The model provides a rational foundation upon which particular theological claims may later be evaluated, requiring no presupposition of revelation. It also seeks to avoid philosophical pitfalls like the God of the Gaps arguments (lack of knowledge means God) by observing natural laws through reason (Because of Knowledge we determine God); while also addressing self-defeating axioms like Nihilism.

detail.abstract: The European Green Deal represents one of the most ambitious policy frameworks aimed at aligning economic transformation with climate neutrality and environmental sustainability. This paper provides an integrated assessment of green growth, green energy, and environmental sustainability within the context of the European Green Deal. Drawing on an extensive review of academic and policy-oriented literature, the study examines how renewable energy expansion, green growth strategies, and sustainability objectives are jointly embedded in the EU's new growth model. The analysis highlights that the Green Deal places green energy at the core of decarbonization while using green growth as a guiding economic narrative to stimulate innovation, competitiveness, and investment. At the same time, the paper identifies key challenges, including implementation capacity, distributional effects, and ongoing debates over whether economic growth can be sufficiently separated from environmental pressure. By analyzing these dimensions together, the study contributes to the literature by offering a holistic perspective on the European Green Deal and provides policy-relevant insights for designing integrated green transition strategies in other regions.

title: Creation of the Bretton-Woods System as a Key Factor of the Development of Auditing

detail.title: Creation of the Bretton-Woods System as a Key Factor of the Development of Auditing
detail.abstract: In July 1944, the Bretton Woods Conference was organized in the USA to establish new principles of the functioning of the global economy after the end of World War II. The decisions made at this event had a significant impact on the formation of the contemporary structure of global finance and economic cooperation. This, in turn, led to an increase in demand for the services of international audit companies and laid the foundation for the development of unified approaches to auditing.

title: From Visibility to Computability in Fiscal Geometry: Standard Deviation and the Admissibility of the Dominant Cloud in Geometric ITI

detail.title: From Visibility to Computability in Fiscal Geometry: Standard Deviation and the Admissibility of the Dominant Cloud in Geometric ITI

detail.abstract:
Fiscal Geometry renders narrative institutional material into geometry-ready interaction records mapped onto an X–Y fiscal plane, making clouds, clusters, and boundary behavior observable. However, geometric visibility does not imply computability: not all visible structure can be reduced to a stable numeric representative suitable for comparison. This paper formalizes an admissibility rule that restricts numerical comparison to the dominant cloud—the densest concentration of interaction records—while retaining secondary clusters and isolated points as an interpretation layer. 

To operationalize admissibility without causal inference or distributional claims, the paper introduces minimal stability diagnostics (dispersion via standard deviation/variance and boundedness via confidence intervals) as non-inferential tests of whether the dominant cloud can support numerical representation. When admissible, the cloud’s axis-projected representative is aligned with Arithmetic ITI on the same scalar axis to derive IDI as a controlled difference between two readings of the same dataset. The result is a restrained computation protocol that prevents indiscriminate quantification while preserving the analytical value of non-computable geometric structure.

title: Smart Railway Track Crack Detection System

detail.title: Smart Railway Track Crack Detection System
detail.abstract: The Smart Railway Track Crack Detection System aims to identify cracks and abnormalities in railway tracks using IoT-based automation. Traditional manual inspection methods are often time-consuming, labor-intensive, and inefficient. This study introduces a cost-effective and efficient solution that integrates various components, such as a GPS, Ultrasonic Sensor, ESP32- CAM, IR Sensor, ESP8266 Wi-Fi Module, and L298N Motor Driver mounted on a motorized chassis. The system was designed to capture real-time images of railway tracks, measure distances, and detect cracks or discontinuities. This integration ensures accurate detection, reduces inspection time, and enhances railway safety, contributing to a more reliable and automated railway maintenance process.

title: GAME THEORY'S HIDDEN ASSUMPTION: Intentionality Homogeneity and the Failure of Corporate Criminal Liability

detail.title: GAME THEORY'S HIDDEN ASSUMPTION: Intentionality Homogeneity and the Failure of Corporate Criminal Liability

detail.abstract:
Von Neumann and Morgenstern (1944), Nash (1951), and Aumann (1976) formalized strategic interaction assuming all players share the same intentionality level. 

This paper identifies that hidden assumption and tests its consequences for corporate criminal liability. Corporations optimize payoffs without recursive social reasoning (Level 1 intentionality). Prosecutors expect cooperation requiring common knowledge formation, shame, and reciprocity (Level 3 intentionality). When these levels differ, Nash equilibrium cannot exist and Aumann's common knowledge cannot form. 

The resulting Dennett-Nash Gap yields an 8.33point systematic advantage for corporations over prosecutors. I test these predictions using Argentina's Law 27401 (2017) and the OECD Anti-Bribery Convention across 41 countries. 

Four structural paradoxes emerge: legal provisions presume corporate "interest," "tolerance," "spontaneous reporting," and "ethical culture"-all Level 3 concepts applied to Level 1 entities. Implementation failure is architecturally necessary, not contingent on enforcement capacity. 

Policy implication: design intentionality-compatible institutions leveraging Level 1 optimization (strict liability, algorithmic monitoring) rather than expecting Level 3 cooperation (ethics codes, voluntary compliance).

title: From Capitalization to Curatorization: A Custodium Protocol for Ecologically Admissible Investment

detail.title: From Capitalization to Curatorization: A Custodium Protocol for Ecologically Admissible Investment

keywords: capitalization; discounted cash flow; ecological realism; planetary boundaries; social reproduction; triple-ledger; custodium; curatorization; investment admissibility; ecological democracy.

detail.abstract: Modern economies govern the future through capitalization: expected cash flows are discounted into present asset values, and investment decisions are legitimized by risk-adjusted returns. This operator coordinates large-scale allocation, yet it systematically displaces ecological constraints and social reproduction into "externalities," deferred liabilities, or unpriced risks. Under ecological realism-where economic activity is embedded in biophysical throughput and bounded by Earthsystem stability-this displacement becomes self-undermining: financial claims on the future can expand while the enabling conditions of futurity erode. The result is not only mispricing but a structural category error: treating the future primarily as a stock of monetizable claims rather than as reproductive capacity. This paper proposes a Custodium Protocol that reorders investment rationality. Projects are admissible only if they satisfy enforceable constraints across three coupled ledgersfinancial, energy/material, and eco-reproduction-and pass three corresponding gates (Eco-Gate, Energy-Gate, Reproduction-Gate). Financial optimization becomes secondary: it applies only among options already proven compatible with the texture of life. The protocol further requires obligation-following (duties persist across ownership and exit), audit 2.0 (financial plus eco/reproduction verification), and automatic correction mechanisms when ledgers deteriorate. Conceptually, the shift is from buying the future to curating futurity: rights to benefit are reframed as authorizations conditioned by duties to maintain the enabling conditions of life.

detail.abstract: This study delves into the public policies implemented by the United Nations (UN), the European Union (EU), and Türkiye in their endeavors to combat the Covid-19 pandemic, which was initially reported to have emerged from the city of Wuhan in the Hubei province of the People's Republic of China in late 2019. Specifically, the study aims to examine and analyze the effectiveness of these actors in managing the Covid-19 and its impact on public health, the economy, and social well-being. Through a comparative lens, the study seeks to shed light on the national and global efforts undertaken by these actors to protect public health and mitigate the socioeconomic consequences of the pandemic. To achieve its objectives, the study begins with providing a comprehensive understanding of the concept of public policy and its relevance in the context of managing public health crises. Furthermore, by providing a historical analysis of past pandemics, it engages in discussions on drawing lessons from previous experiences for the current pandemic's management and policymaking. Subsequently, the strategies that pursued by UN, the EU and Türkiye in tackling the Covid-19 outbreak are critically examined and evaluated. In order to make a comparison between different political organizational levels (international organization, regional cooperation, and nation-state) in combating the pandemic, these actors have been selected. The study assesses the efficacy, effectiveness, adaptability, problem-solving capacity, and establishment of global solidarity through an evaluation framework, which encompasses various criteria by using qualitative analysis methods. Subsequently, the study seeks to offer nuanced insights into the strengths, limitations, and lessons learned from the public policies formulated and implemented by these actors during the Covid-19 pandemic. By undertaking this academic inquiry, the study would contribute to the scholarly surrounding pandemic management and public policy formulation. It also contributes to the understanding of the effectiveness and impact of public policies in the context of a global health crisis and provides a background for public health policy makers and stakeholders. The analyzed public policies show that the actors basically pursue similar policies, but there are differences in terms of timing.

title: The Psychological Ceiling of AI Adoption: Why the AI Bubble is a Social Phenomenon, Not a Technical One

detail.title: The Psychological Ceiling of AI Adoption: Why the AI Bubble is a Social Phenomenon, Not a Technical One

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None. This research was conducted independently without any financial support or conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical analysis without empirical data collection, human subjects, or experimental interventions.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This article argues that the evolution of artificial intelligence is not limited primarily by technical constraints, but by a psychological ceiling of the human user.

Based on Leta Hollingworth's observations on the social isolation of gifted individuals and modern research on the perception of competence as a threat, we argue that most people cannot maintain comfortable interactions with an intelligence they perceive as significantly superior to their own.

When AI models reach an IQ equivalent of about 120, further increases in capabilities do not expand the market, but contract it - generating cognitive discomfort that causes the average user to migrate to simpler alternatives. We propose a reinterpretation of the logistic adoption curve: the asymptote is socially imposed, not technically. We estimate the emergence of a two-tier market: a cognitive elite (2-5%) capable of symbiotic human-AI partnership and a majority (>95%) oriented towards one-way interactions and simplified products.

The article includes testable predictions for the period 2026-2028: bimodal segregation in usage, avoidance of complex tasks correlated with education, explicit preference for simplification in populations with average IQ, and differential adoption across cognitive cohorts. 

Finally, we introduce the concept of Homo Symbioticus as a possible direction of long-term evolution: a cognitively adapted minority that will play a central role in the future socio-economic structure, based on the ability to deeply collaborate with artificial intelligences.

title: Influence of Live Streamers on Modern Marketing strategies: Opportunities and Challenges
affiliations: University of Kolkata

detail.title: Influence of Live Streamers on Modern Marketing strategies: Opportunities and Challenges
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of live streaming platforms has transformed digital marketing by enabling brands to communicate with consumers in real time through interactive and highly engaging content formats. Live streamers, viewed as authentic and relatable, have emerged as influential intermediaries who shape consumer perception, trust, and purchase intention. This study investigates the role of live streamers in driving consumer engagement and evaluates their impact on modern marketing strategies, with a particular focus on the growing Indian live commerce market. Drawing on a mixed-method approach that integrates industry reports with primary survey data from digitally active consumers aged 18–35, the research identifies key behavioural trends, opportunities, and challenges associated with live-streaming-based marketing. Findings reveal that real-time interactions significantly enhance brand recall, stimulate impulse purchasing, and foster para-social relationships that strengthen consumer loyalty. However, challenges such as audience saturation, inconsistent content quality, ethical concerns, and difficulties in measuring ROI persist. The study underscores the importance of authenticity, transparent engagement metrics, and culturally adaptive strategies for brands seeking to leverage live commerce. It concludes by highlighting the need for interdisciplinary research to further explore the psychological and sociocultural implications of streamer-driven marketing.

title: Smart Olympics, Smart Cities：Strategic Lessons from Past Games for the LA 2028 Vision
affiliations: California State University

detail.title: Smart Olympics, Smart Cities：Strategic Lessons from Past Games for the LA 2028 Vision
detail.abstract: The Olympic Games have long served as catalysts for urban transformation, with host cities leveraging the global event to accelerate infrastructure upgrades, technological innovation, and reforms in governance systems. This paper aims to trace the historical evolution of 'Smart Olympics' concept, systematically reviewing and analyzing the successes and failures of previous Olympic Games in the construction of smart infrastructure and digital transformation. By integrating documentary research, news reports, and field investigations, it selects the 2008 Beijing Olympics, the 2012 London Olympics, the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, and the 2024 Paris Olympics as typical cases to explore their smart practices and positive outcomes under diverse political, economic, and urban contexts. At the same time, it examines the shortcomings and challenges exposed during the preparation and hosting of the 1976 Montreal Olympics, the 2004 Athens Olympics, and the 2016 Rio Olympics, identifies its potential and key issues in smart development, and proposes forward-looking preliminary strategic recommendations, aiming to provide insights for the sustainable and intelligent transformation of future large-scale events.

title: The Departed: Italian Migration and the American Mafia
affiliations: Bocconi University, Bocconi University - BAFFI Center on International Markets, Money, and Regulation and

detail.title: The Departed: Italian Migration and the American Mafia
detail.abstract: We document the transplantation of the Sicilian Mafia to the United States in the 1920s, when a large-scale repression campaign in Italy targeted Mafia strongholds and forced many Mafiosi to migrate, and study the resulting short- and long-term effects across neighborhoods in U.S. cities. Using newly linked administrative and historical data from the U.S. Census, Social Security records, and declassified files of the Federal Bureau of Narcotics, we show that neighborhoods hosting enclaves of migrants from Sicilian Mafia strongholds targeted by the repression later became centers of Italo-American Mafia activity. These neighborhoods experienced higher violence, incarceration, and financial exclusion in the short run, but higher income, employment, and educational attainment in the long run. The results suggest that while the arrival of organized criminal networks initially intensified conflict and exclusion, their subsequent consolidation generated localized economic benefits, helping to explain the long-term resilience and persistence of organized crime.

title: How Fast Does the Fed Reach DeFi? Pass-Through and Settlement Lags in Stablecoin Yields

detail.title: How Fast Does the Fed Reach DeFi? Pass-Through and Settlement Lags in Stablecoin Yields
detail.abstract: Decentralized Finance (DeFi) stablecoin markets increasingly function as a shadow overnight dollar system, yet the speed at which U.S. monetary policy transmits to on-chain yields remains unclear. Focusing on the recent "High-for-Long" regime (2023–2025), I quantify this pass-through using an ordered VAR framework on daily Aave V3 rates for USDC and USDT. Results show that DeFi yields are tightly anchored to the Federal Funds Rate (and SOFR), which challenges the "crypto-decoupling" narrative. However, transmission is not instantaneous; it exhibits a distinct T+3 structural latency. This lag is universal across both compliant USDC and unregulated USDT, indicating an infrastructural and systemic friction rather than issuer-specific constraints. Robustness and placebo tests rule out protocol outliers, macroeconomic trends, and weekend effects, attributing the delay instead to legacy settlement and execution cycles in traditional banking rails. These findings demonstrate that despite algorithmic immediacy, DeFi remains physically throttled by fiat infrastructure. Consequently, modernizing payment rails is as critical as issuer regulation for improving on-chain capital efficiency.

title: The Quiet Architecture of Autonomy: The Line Between Persuasion and Manipulation

detail.title: The Quiet Architecture of Autonomy: The Line Between Persuasion and Manipulation
detail.abstract:
Institutions rarely collapse from malice or incompetence; they drift quietly when emotional synchronization replaces proportion, and when narrative pressure eclipses interpretation. To the Educated presents a neutral, theory-driven account of how institutions lose clarity, suppress internal autonomy, and produce environments where dissent becomes dangerous, nuance becomes costly, and silence becomes rational. Drawing from high-salience case studies of public intellectuals who experienced institutional pressure firsthand, the manuscript offers a structural model of institutional drift and a corresponding recovery framework based on cognitive pluralism, incentive realignment, interpretive reopening, and feedback-loop restoration.
Rather than diagnosing partisan failure, the book maps universal patterns of institutional behavior—showing how drift emerges, how it becomes self-reinforcing, and ultimately how institutions return to proportion, humility, and functional sanity. Written directly to the educated class who staff, run, and influence modern institutions, To the Educated is a theory of how drift occurs and a practical blueprint for how institutions regain their mind.

title: Crime and Prices: Evidence From Thefts of Expensive Precious Metal
affiliations: , London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Centre for Economic Performance (CEP) and London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Centre for Economic Performance (CEP)

detail.title: Crime and Prices: Evidence From Thefts of Expensive Precious Metal
detail.abstract: We study whether economic incentives matter for crime in a novel way, through study of expensive precious metal thefts by thieves stealing catalytic converters. We combine sharp, plausibly exogenous variation in the prices of precious metals embedded in converters with newly assembled U.S. data and multiple research designs. We show that phenomenally fast increases in precious metal prices generated a sizeable and rapid rise in auto-part thefts, while subsequent price declines and policy responses quickly reversed this pattern. The resulting boom-and-bust dynamics provide clean evidence that both demand- and supply-side economic forces shape property crime and inform targeted deterrence policies.

title: Public Insurance and Demand for Private Healthcare
affiliations: University of Warwick, IIM Calcutta and City College of New York

detail.title: Public Insurance and Demand for Private Healthcare
detail.abstract: Establishment of public–private partnerships is an emerging model in health care delivery. This study evaluates a pioneering social health insurance program in India that enables eligible households to access private hospitals for tertiary care services free of cost, but does not build more facilities. Leveraging policy discontinuities at state borders, we identify the program’s causal effects on utilization of private facilities and associated out-of-pocket expenditures. The results indicate a pronounced substitution effect induced by relative price changes: the program substantially increases the incidence of deliveries in private hospitals while significantly reducing out-of-pocket spending. However, we find no statistically significant effects on fertility or a key health outcome, infant mortality.

detail.title: The Minimum Wage and Inequality Between Groups
detail.abstract: Using 1979-2019 Current Population Survey data, we study the effect of state and federal minimum wage policies on gender, race, and ethnic inequality. We find that minimum wages substantially reduce intergroup wage inequality at least up to the 20th wage percentile, with no evidence of adverse employment effects. We conduct counterfactual simulations of between-group inequality due to minimum wage changes since 1979. Declines in the real minimum wage in the 1980s slowed progress in narrowing between-group inequality. Relatively small changes in minimum wages during 1989-1998 and 1998-2007 meant little role for the minimum wage over those time spans. Since 2007, several states have steeply raised their minimum wages, especially raising Hispanics’ relative wages, because they earn low wages and reside disproportionately in those states. Finally, we find that raising the federal minimum wage to $12/hour in 2020 dollars ($14.49 in 2025Q2 dollars) would reduce existing between-group wage gaps below the 15th percentile by 25-50%.

title: Welfare Reform: Consequences for the Children
affiliations: Aarhus University - Department of Economics and Business Economics, Aarhus University - Department of Economics and Business Economics and University of Wisconsin-Madison

detail.title: Welfare Reform: Consequences for the Children
detail.abstract: This paper uses register-based data to analyze the consequences of a recent major Danish welfare reform for children’s academic performance and well-being. In addition to work requirements, the reform brought about considerable reductions in welfare transfers. We implement a comparative event study that contrasts outcomes for individuals on welfare at the time of reform announcement before and after the implementation of the reform with the parallel development in outcomes for an uncontaminated comparison group, namely those on welfare exactly one year prior. Our analysis documents that mothers’ propensity to receive welfare decreased somewhat as a consequence of the reform, just as we observe a small increase in hours worked. At the same time, we do not detect negative effects on children’s short-run academic performance. We do find small negative effects on children’s self-reported school well-being and document substantial upticks in reports to child protective services for children exposed to the reform.
